thread:
carmen: opened a quick PR to tidy up SDK examples around streaming + pagination + retries. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4321

jun: nice, thanks for doing this. which SDK versions are we targeting?

carmen: targeting py 0.9.x, ts 1.4.x, go 0.7.x. main goals: unify streaming handler patterns, show idiomatic retry/backoff, and fix the pagination cursor field (was `next_cursor` -> `cursor`). also added a small migration note.

mike: skimmed. Go example looks good functionally but small nit: use `context.WithTimeout` in the top-level example so people don't leak goroutines.

carmen: good call, added ctx example. PTAL at the Go block below.

jun: also please add a short note for the async iterator change in Python — people upgrading might still be using `for chunk in stream():` instead of `async for chunk in stream():`.

carmen: done. Added a migration snippet and highlighted sync->async change.

zara: docs-bot: checklist: run `./tools/snippet-lint` and `make docs-build` before merging. Also we need a smoke test for the TS streaming example in CI.

carmen: acknowledged. I added a lightweight smoke test under `examples/ts/stream-smoke.test.ts` that just asserts we get a single message back from the mock.

samantha: on the retry example, can we prefer exponential backoff with jitter? People copy/paste the naive linear backoff and it causes thundering herds.

carmen: yes, switched to a small helper in all three snippets: `retryWithJitter` (pseudo impl in the docs).

jun: can you paste the TypeScript snippet here so I can quickly review the handler shape?

carmen: sure — TS streaming example I added:

```ts
// client is an instance of RedwoodClient from @redwood-inference/sdk
const res = await client.responses.stream({
  model: 'open-rtx-legacy',
  input: 'Tail the logs and summarize errors',
  onMessage: (evt) => {
    if (evt.type === 'delta') console.log(evt.delta.text);
    if (evt.type === 'done') console.log('stream finished');
  },
  retry: retryWithJitter,
  pagination: { pageSize: 100, cursorParam: 'cursor' },
});
```

mike: looks good. minor comment: use `await res.finished()` is that an API? maybe we want `await res.waitForCompletion()` per current SDK naming.

carmen: thanks — updated to `await res.waitForCompletion()` across the examples.

tyler: about the cursor param rename: make sure we add a short migration note in the changelog and in the top of the pagination doc, e.g. `If you used next_cursor, rename to cursor and update your client call` — some customers have infra scripts that parse docs for config keys.

carmen: added a migration snippet at the top of the pagination guide and referenced the changelog entry.

zara: also, link fix: the old embedding guide link was broken after the site move. Did you update that?

carmen: yes — replaced the broken link and ran a linkcheck job locally.

samantha: small wording nits in the python snippet: use `async with client.stream_responses(...) as stream:` pattern to make cleanup explicit.

carmen: updated Python block. here's the Python example I included:

```py
# async streaming example
async with client.stream_responses(model='meta-short', input='Summarize latest alerts') as stream:
    async for msg in stream:
        if msg.type == 'delta':
            print(msg.delta.text)
        elif msg.type == 'done':
            print('done')
    await stream.wait_for_completion()
```

jun: perfect. that `async with` pattern helps on cancellation.

mike: Go snippet LGTM with the ctx timeout change. Can you show the Go block you added?

carmen: Go example (shortened):

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.StreamResponses(ctx, &StreamParams{Model: "meta-short", Input: "Summarize"})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatalf("stream start: %v", err)
}
for {
    msg, err := stream.Recv()
    if err == io.EOF {
        break
    }
    if err != nil {
        log.Printf("recv err: %v", err)
        break
    }
    switch msg.Type {
    case DeltaMessage:
        fmt.Print(msg.Delta.Text)
    case DoneMessage:
        fmt.Println("done")
    }
}
stream.Close()
```

zara: cool. last ops ask: can we include a tiny perf note that streaming + large page sizes can increase memory usage on clients? a single line in the pagination doc would be enough.

carmen: added one-liner under `Performance considerations`.

jun: ready to review final changes. I can approve TS and Python after one more pass; I'll leave Go to Mike.

mike: I'll give a quick approve after addressing the ctx nit.

zara: docs-bot: moving PR to `review/ready` once CI passes.

carmen: thanks all — I'll wait for CI and then merge. If anything else pops up I'll post here. :sparkles:
